available_assertion.objects: The unique discriminant-six principally polarized quaternionic component X6 and its fixed three-mark Hauptmodul, with the modular forms s2,s3,s5,s6 and Igusa invariants.
available_assertion.hypotheses: The actual principal datum maps to this component through the separately supplied A001 coarse quotient. Retain the exact published intersection and divisor assertions as inputs.
available_assertion.quantifiers: The stated global identities and the specified CM(-4) and CM(-24) evaluations on this component.
available_assertion.parameter_range: Characteristic zero, same point and weight conventions. Evaluate ratios only when their denominators are nonzero.
available_assertion.uniformity: No other quaternionic discriminant or arbitrary polarization is covered.
available_assertion.constants: The exact constants in published equations13–14 and Examples29–30; no use of the CM(-19) value81/64.
available_assertion.normalizations: j(CM-4)=0, j(CM-3)=infinity, j(CM-24)=-16/27; Siegel weights4,6,10,12 and projective weights2,3,5,6; Igusa weights1,2,3,5.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: Do not infer global ratio shapes from finite evaluations. Product intersection is principally polarized, not merely an isogeny. No BG explicit conic map or product-isomorphism proof is imported.
available_assertion.limit_order: First retain published global shapes and intersection inputs, then determine constants; subsequent weighted conversion and Q-definition keep their separate premises.
